paragraphs.sourceText: In this section there are three passages followed by fourteen multiple choice questions. For each multiple choice question, there are four suggested answers marked A, B, C and D. Choose the one that you think is the best answer and mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节由三篇文章组成，后面是十四道多项选择题。对于每个多项选择题，有四个建议答案，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。选择您认为最佳答案的一个，并将您的答案标记在答题表二上。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Buck did not read the newspapers, or he would have known that trouble was brewing, not alone for himself, but for every tidewater dog, strong of muscle and with warm, long hair, from Puget Sound to San Diego. Because men, groping in the Arctic darkness, had found a yellow metal, and because steamship and transportation companies were booming the find, thousands of men were rushing into the Northland. These men wanted dogs, and the dogs they wanted were heavy dogs, with strong muscles by which to toil, and furry coats to protect them from the frost.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 巴克没有读报纸，否则他就会知道麻烦正在酝酿之中，这不仅是为了他自己，也是为了从普吉特海湾到圣地亚哥的每一条肌肉发达、长着温暖的长毛的潮水狗。因为人们在北极的黑暗中摸索，发现了一种黄色金属，而且由于轮船和运输公司的蓬勃发展，成千上万的人涌入北国。这些人想要狗，而他们想要的狗是重型狗，有强壮的肌肉可以用来劳作，有毛茸茸的皮毛可以保护它们免受霜冻。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) Buck lived at a big house in the sun-kissed Santa Clara Valley. Judge Miller’s place, it was called. It stood back from the road, half hidden among the trees, through which glimpses could be caught of the wide cool veranda that ran around its four sides. The house was approached by gravelled driveways which wound about through wide-spreading lawns and under the interlacing boughs of tall poplars (杨树) .At the rear things were on even a more spacious scale than at the front. There were great stables, where a dozen grooms and boys held forth, rows of vine-clad servants’ cottages, an endless and orderly array of outhouses, long grape arbors, green pastures, orchards, and berry patches. Then there was the pumping plant for the artesian well, and the big cement tank where Judge Miller’s boys took their morning plunge and kept cool in the hot afternoon.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 巴克住在阳光明媚的圣克拉拉山谷的一所大房子里。它被称为米勒法官的住所。它远离道路，半隐藏在树林中，透过树木可以瞥见环绕其四个侧面的宽阔凉爽的阳台。房子前面有一条碎石车道，蜿蜒穿过宽阔的草坪，在高大的杨树交错的树枝下。后面的东西比前面更宽敞。这里有巨大的马厩，十几个马夫和男孩在那里忙碌，一排排藤蔓覆盖的仆人小屋，一望无际、井然有序的外屋、长长的葡萄架、绿色牧场、果园和浆果园。然后还有自流井的抽水装置和大水泥罐，米勒法官的孩子们早上在这里跳水，并在炎热的下午保持凉爽。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) And over this great demesne (自用地) Buck ruled. Here he was born, and here he had lived the four years of his life. It was true, there were other dogs. There could not but be other dogs on so vast a place, but they did not count. They came and went, resided in the populous kennels, or lived obscurely in the recesses of the house after the fashion of Toots, the Japanese pug, or Ysabel, the Mexican hairless, — strange creatures that rarely put nose out of doors or set foot to ground. On the other hand, there were the fox terriers, a score of them at least, who yelped fearful promises at Toots and Ysabel looking out of the windows at them and protected by a legion of housemaids armed with brooms and mops.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 巴克统治着这片自用地。他在这里出生，在这里度过了四年的人生。确实如此，还有其他狗。这么大的地方，不可能没有别的狗，但它们不算数。它们来了又走，住在人口众多的狗舍里，或者像日本哈巴狗图茨或墨西哥无毛犬伊莎贝尔一样隐秘地住在房子的隐蔽处，这些奇怪的生物很少把鼻子伸出门外或踏上地面。另一方面，还有猎狐犬，至少有二十只，它们对图茨和伊莎贝尔发出可怕的承诺，图茨和伊莎贝尔看着窗外的它们，并受到一群手持扫帚和拖把的女仆的保护。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) But Buck was neither house-dog nor kennel-dog. The whole realm was his. He plunged into the swimming tank or went hunting with the Judge’s sons; he escorted Mollie and Alice, the Judge’s daughters, on long twilight or early morning rambles; on wintry nights he lay at the Judge’s feet before the roaring library fire; he carried the Judge's grandsons on his back, or rolled them in the grass, and guarded their footsteps through wild adventures down to the fountain in the stable yard, and even beyond, where the paddocks were, and the berry patches. Among the terriers he stalked imperiously, and Toots and Ysabel he utterly ignored, for he was king, — king over all creeping, crawling, flying things of Judge Miller’s place, humans included.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 但是巴克既不是看家狗，也不是养狗人。整个领域都是他的。他跳进游泳池或者和法官的儿子们一起去打猎；他护送法官的女儿莫莉和爱丽丝进行漫长的黄昏或清晨漫步。冬天的夜晚，他躺在图书馆熊熊燃烧的炉火前，躺在法官脚边。他把法官的孙子背在背上，或者把他们滚到草地上，通过疯狂的冒险守护着他们的脚步，一直到马厩院子里的喷泉，甚至更远的地方，那里有围场和浆果地。在猎犬中，他专横地跟踪，而图茨和伊莎贝尔则被他完全无视，因为他是国王——米勒法官那里所有爬行、爬行、飞行生物的国王，包括人类。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) His father, Elmo, a huge St.Bernard, had been the Judge’s inseparable companion, and Buck bid fair to follow in the way of his father. He was not so large, — he weighed only one hundred and forty pounds, — for his mother, Shep, had been a Scotch shepherd dog. Nevertheless, one hundred and forty pounds, to which was added the dignity that comes of good living and universal respect, enabled him to carry himself in right royal fashion. During the four years since his puppyhood he had lived the life of a sated (饱享的) aristocrat; he had a fine pride in himself, was even a trifle egotistical, as country gentlemen sometimes become because of their insular situation. But he had saved himself by not becoming a mere pampered house-dog. Hunting and kindred outdoor delights had kept down the fat and hardened his muscles; and to him, as to the cold-tubbing races, the love of water had been a tonic and a health preserver.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 他的父亲埃尔莫是一只巨大的圣伯纳犬，是法官形影不离的伴侣，巴克也公平地追随了他父亲的道路。他个头不大——体重只有一百四十磅——因为他的母亲谢普是一只苏格兰牧羊犬。尽管如此，一百四十英镑，再加上美好生活和普遍尊重带来的尊严，使他能够以正确的王室风范行事。从幼年起的四年里，他过着饱享贵族生活的日子。他对自己非常自豪，甚至有点自负，就像乡下绅士有时因为他们的孤立处境而变得如此。但他拯救了自己，没有成为一只被宠坏的看门狗。狩猎和类似的户外活动减少了他的脂肪，增强了他的肌肉。对他来说，就像在冷水池比赛中一样，对水的热爱是一种补品和保健品。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) And this was the manner of Buck in the fall of 1897, when the Klondike strike dragged men from all the world into the frozen North. But Buck did not read the newspapers, and he did not know that Manuel, one of the gardener's helpers, was an undesirable acquaintance. Manuel had one besetting sin. He loved to play lottery. Also, in his gambling, he had one besetting weakness — faith in a system; and this made his damnation certain. For to play a system requires money, while the wages of a gardener’s helper do not lap over the needs of a wife and numerous progeny.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 这就是 1897 年秋天巴克的做法，当时克朗代克罢工将世界各地的人们拖到了冰天雪地的北方。但巴克不看报纸，也不知道园丁的助手之一曼纽尔是个不受欢迎的熟人。曼努埃尔有一项困扰他的罪。他喜欢玩彩票。此外，在赌博中，他还有一个致命的弱点——对制度的信仰；这使他的诅咒变得确定无疑。因为玩一个系统需要钱，而园丁帮手的工资还不足以满足妻子和众多后代的需要。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Early this winter, the hundreds of climbers making plans for spring-summit attempts on Mount Qomolangma suddenly faced a new set of rules. In December, the Nepalese government decreed that it would no longer issue permits to blind, solo, or double-amputee mountaineers for any of its high peaks. Furthermore, all expeditions would have to employ at least one Sherpa (夏尔巴人向导) and would be forbidden from using helicopters to reach high camps.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 今年冬初，数百名计划春季登顶珠穆朗玛峰的登山者突然面临着一套新的规则。 12月，尼泊尔政府颁布法令，不再向盲人、独行者或双截肢登山者发放攀登任何高峰的许可证。此外，所有探险队都必须雇用至少一名夏尔巴人（夏尔巴人），并且禁止使用直升机到达高处营地。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) The regulations fit a pattern established by Nepal’s Ministry of Tourism, which in the past few years has issued a series of proclamations — climbers must announce plans to set records, trekkers must carry location beacons — that suggest improved management of its high-altitude peaks. Each new declaration generates a rush of international news reports about authorities making strides toward addressing safety at the top of the world. The truth is a lot more complicated.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 这些规定符合尼泊尔旅游部制定的模式，该部在过去几年发布了一系列公告——登山者必须宣布创造纪录的计划，徒步旅行者必须携带定位信标——建议改善对其高海拔山峰的管理。每一项新的声明都会引发大量国际新闻报道，报道有关当局在解决世界之巅安全问题方面取得的进展。事实要复杂得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) Mountaineering is big business in Nepal. Industry experts estimate that it generates some $26.5 million in tourism income each year, with around $l1 million of that coming from Qomolangma climbers alone. The enduring obsession of the Western media with tragic deaths on these far-off snowy peaks has resulted in a lot of free marketing. Nepal’s Ministry of Tourism, perhaps concerned that all the morbid tales might drive climbers to Qomolangma’s less used Chinese side, has gained some control of that narrative by broadcasting more positive developments through the Nepalese press. But the rules announced to date would do nothing to mitigate the dangers of climbing Qomolangma even if Nepal had the resources and conviction to enforce them, which it doesn’t.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 登山在尼泊尔是一项大生意。业内专家估计，它每年产生约2650万美元的旅游收入，其中约110万美元仅来自珠穆朗玛峰登山者。西方媒体对这些遥远雪峰上的悲惨死亡的持久痴迷导致了许多免费营销。尼泊尔旅游部或许担心所有这些病态的故事可能会驱使登山者前往珠穆朗玛峰较少使用的中国一侧，因此通过尼泊尔媒体广播了更多积极的事态发展，从而在一定程度上控制了这种说法。但迄今为止宣布的规则无助于减轻攀登珠穆朗玛峰的危险，即使尼泊尔有资源和信念来执行这些规则，但尼泊尔却没有。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) Making a huge, hugely popular mountain safer is possible. On Alaska’s Denali, fulltime climbing rangers conduct safety checks of many teams and are mobilized for rescue operations. On Argentina’s Aconcagua, rangers patrol all high camps, and until recently, permit fees included the cost of helicopter rescues. Adopting similar policies in Nepal would be a good start. A longer list of true reforms would include ordering all climbers to have previously summited a 7,000-meter peak, requiring non-guides working above Base Camp to take a course at the Khumbu Climbing Center (hundreds have done so since it was founded in 2003), and capping the total number of climbers on the mountain at 500 per season, including support staff. That last policy would both reduce dangerous crowding and help keep the mountain clean.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 让一座广受欢迎的巨大山峰更加安全是可能的。在阿拉斯加的麦金利峰，全职登山护林员对许多团队进行安全检查，并被动员进行救援行动。在阿根廷的阿空加瓜，护林员在所有高地营地巡逻，直到最近，许可证费用还包括直升机救援的费用。在尼泊尔采取类似的政策将是一个良好的开端。一份更长的真正改革清单将包括命令所有登山者之前都曾登顶过 7,000 米的山峰，要求在大本营上方工作的非导游在昆布攀岩中心参加课程（自 2003 年成立以来已有数百人参加），并将每个登山季的登山者总数限制在 500 人，其中包括支持人员。最后一项政策既可以减少危险的拥挤，又有助于保持山上的清洁。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) Unfortunately, these kinds of rules are less likely than ever to be instituted on Qomolangma, owing to the rise of budget guiding companies. Beginning in the early 1990s, Western outfitters established commercial mountaineering on the Nepal side of the peak by attracting clients willing to pay as much as $65,000 to be guided to the summit. That business model dominated for more than two decades, bringing an estimated 9,000 paying climbers to Base Camp. Consequently, Qomolangma earned a reputation as a magnet for the rich, ambitious, and inexperienced.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 不幸的是，由于预算指导公司的兴起，在珠穆朗玛峰上制定此类规则的可能性比以往任何时候都小。从 20 世纪 90 年代初开始，西方旅行用品商通过吸引愿意支付高达 65,000 美元的导游登顶的客户，在珠穆朗玛峰的尼泊尔一侧建立了商业登山活动。这种商业模式主导了二十多年，为大本营带来了大约 9,000 名付费登山者。因此，珠穆朗玛峰赢得了吸引富人、雄心勃勃和缺乏经验的人的声誉。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) As in many markets, savvy entrepreneurs saw opportunities for disruption. Lower-cost guiding companies, some founded by Westerners and others by Nepalese, slowly gained attraction by offering Qomolangma climbs for as little as a third of the going rate among high-end outfitters. Then came 2014,when 16 Sherpas died after a serac (冰塔) collapsed onto the Khumbu Icefall, part of the main route from Base Camp to Camp I. In the wake of that tragedy, a small group of Sherpas demanded that the Nepalese government establish regulations that would improve working conditions, increase pay, boost life-insurance coverage, and provide a funeral stipend. Ultimately, Sherpas received a bit more insurance — the minimum payout was doubled from $5,500 to $11,000 — but not much else.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 与许多市场一样，精明的企业家看到了颠覆的机会。成本较低的导游公司（有些是西方人创办的，有些是尼泊尔人创办的）通过提供珠穆朗玛峰攀登服务而慢慢获得了吸引力，价格仅为高端旅行用品商现行价格的三分之一。然后到了 2014 年，昆布冰川上的一座冰塔倒塌，造成 16 名夏尔巴人死亡。昆布冰川是从大本营到一号营地的主要路线的一部分。这场悲剧发生后，一小群夏尔巴人要求尼泊尔政府制定法规，改善工作条件、增加工资、提高人寿保险覆盖范围并提供丧葬津贴。最终，夏尔巴人获得了更多的保险——最低赔付额从 5,500 美元翻倍至 11,000 美元——但除此之外就没有太多了。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) Partly in response to media attention of these events, Nepali-owned guiding companies have continued to gain influence and market share on Qomolangma. The shift away from foreign control of the mountain is welcomed by many in the climbing community. Another positive development: lower-cost operators are increasing diversity on Qomolangma, attracting climbers from China’s and India’s burgeoning middle classes with aggressive pricing. Based on numbers from the Himalayan Database, in 2010, four Indian and eight Chinese climbers attempted the mountain, just 6 percent of the total. Last year, Chinese and Indian clients accounted for 60 of the 199 Nepal-side summits.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7)尼泊尔本土导游公司在珠穆朗玛峰的影响力和市场份额不断扩大，部分原因是为了回应媒体对这些事件的关注。外国对这座山的控制的转变受到登山界许多人的欢迎。另一个积极的进展是：低成本运营商正在增加珠穆朗玛峰的多样性，以激进的定价吸引来自中国和印度新兴中产阶级的登山者。根据喜马拉雅山数据库的数据，2010年，有四名印度登山者和八名中国登山者尝试攀登这座山，仅占总数的6%。去年，在199场尼方峰会中，中国和印度客户占了60场。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) Unfortunately, in the absence of substantive government oversight, some of the budget companies are making Qomolangma more dangerous by flooding the already overcrowded route with novice climbers led by inexperienced guides. Any operators charging less for guided climbs are prone to bolster profits through scale, booking dozens of clients on expeditions. (The most respected outfitters set a maximum of ten.)Putting aside 2014’s tragedy and 2015’s earthquake-induced avalanche, which killed at least 17 people at Base Camp,12 of the 17 climber deaths on the South Col route between 2011 and 2017 appear to have been clients of budget outfitters.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 不幸的是，在政府缺乏实质性监督的情况下，一些廉价公司在缺乏经验的导游带领下涌入了已经人满为患的路线，让珠穆朗玛峰变得更加危险。任何对导游攀登收取较低费用的运营商都倾向于通过规模来增加利润，为数十名客户预订探险活动。 （最受尊敬的户外用品商规定最多 10 人。） 撇开 2014 年的悲剧和 2015 年地震引发的雪崩（导致大本营至少 17 人死亡）不谈，2011 年至 2017 年间南坳路线上死亡的 17 名登山者中，有 12 人似乎是廉价户外用品商的客户。

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) During last year’s peak season, Kathmandu-based Seven Summit Treks, known for bringing large groups of climbers to Qomolangma, allegedly promoted a young support staffer named Sange to guide Qomolangma and assigned him to an older Pakistani client. The pair reached the summit late in the day and got into trouble on their descent. They had to be rescued by experienced Sherpas from another Nepalese outfitter. Sange later had all his fingers amputated due to severe frostbite.
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 在去年的旺季期间，总部位于加德满都的七峰徒步旅行公司（Seven Summit Treks）以带领大批登山者前往珠穆朗玛峰而闻名，据称，该组织提拔了一名名叫桑格（Sange）的年轻后勤人员来指导珠穆朗玛峰，并将他指派给一位年长的巴基斯坦客户。两人在当天晚些时候到达山顶，但在下撤时遇到了麻烦。他们必须由另一家尼泊尔旅行用品商的经验丰富的夏尔巴人营救。桑格后来因严重冻伤而全部手指被截肢。

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) Veteran guides are reacting to all this in different ways. Adrian Ballinger, founder of the California outfitter Alpenglow, has abandoned the Nepal side of Qomolangma and is instead leading teams from China. As he explained it, the higher risk from natural dangers (avalanches, seracs, crevasses), the low standards of other outfitters, and Nepal’s mismanagement add up to an unacceptable environment. Several other prominent guides have come to the same conclusion, including Austrian Lukas Furtenbach. Others are staying put. International Mountain Guides co-owner Eric Simonson, whose first expedition on Qomolangma was in 1982, insists that upgrades in route-making through the Khumbu Icefall, and the establishment of dual ropes in areas prone to bottlenecks, have made the Nepal side safer, even as the crowds have grown.
paragraphs.translationZh: (10) 经验丰富的导游对这一切做出了不同的反应。加州服装公司 Alpenglow 的创始人阿德里安·巴林格 (Adrian Ballinger) 放弃了珠穆朗玛峰的尼泊尔一侧，转而领导来自中国的团队。正如他所解释的那样，自然灾害（雪崩、冰塔、裂缝）带来的较高风险、其他户外用品供应商的低标准以及尼泊尔的管理不善，共同构成了令人无法接受的环境。其他几位著名导游也得出了同样的结论，其中包括奥地利人卢卡斯·富滕巴赫 (Lukas Furtenbach)。其他人则留在原地。国际登山指南共同所有人埃里克·西蒙森 (Eric Simonson) 于 1982 年首次登上珠穆朗玛峰，他坚称，尽管人群有所增加，但昆布冰川路线规划的升级，以及在容易出现瓶颈的地区设置双绳索，使得尼泊尔一侧更加安全。

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) Qomolangma remains the ultimate conquest for many climbers. And while most embrace the risk of high-altitude mountaineering, few understand that the biggest dangers are all too often the result of economics, not the forces of nature. Ultimately, the top priority of many tourism officials and outfitters isn’t safety. It’s the bottom line.
paragraphs.translationZh: (11) 珠穆朗玛峰仍然是许多登山者的终极征服目标。虽然大多数人都接受高海拔登山的风险，但很少有人明白，最大的危险往往是经济的结果，而不是自然的力量。最终，许多旅游官员和旅行用品商的首要任务并不是安全。这是底线。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Vast stretches of central Asia feel eerily uninhabited. Fly at 30,000 feet over the southern part of the former Soviet Union and there are long moments when no town or road or field is visible from your window. The landscape of stark desert, trackless steppe (大草原), and rugged mountains seems to swallow up anything human. It is little surprise, then, that this region remains largely unknown to most archaeologists.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 中亚大片地区荒无人烟。在前苏联南部 30,000 英尺高空飞行时，有很长一段时间，从窗户里看不到城镇、道路或田野。荒凉的沙漠、无路可走的大草原和崎岖的山脉似乎吞噬了人类的一切。因此，大多数考古学家对这个地区仍然一无所知也就不足为奇了。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) Wandering bands and tribes roamed this immense area for 5,000 years, herding goat, sheep, cattle, and horses across immense steppes, through narrow valleys, and over high snowy passes. They left occasional tombs that survived the ages, and on rare occasions settled down and built towns or even cities. But for the most part, these peoples left behind few physical traces of their origins, beliefs, or ways of life. What we know of these nomadic pastoralists comes mainly from their periodic forays into India, the Middle East, and China, where they often wreaked havoc and earned a fearsome reputation as enemies of urban life.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 流浪部落和部落在这片广阔的地区漫游了 5000 年，放牧山羊、绵羊、牛和马，穿过广阔的草原，穿过狭窄的山谷，越过高高的雪山隘口。他们偶尔留下了历经岁月而幸存下来的坟墓，并且在极少数情况下定居下来并建造了城镇甚至城市。但在大多数情况下，这些民族几乎没有留下任何有关其起源、信仰或生活方式的痕迹。我们对这些游牧民族的了解主要来自他们对印度、中东和中国的定期入侵，他们经常在这些地方造成严重破坏，并赢得了城市生活敌人的可怕声誉。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) In the past century, scholars criticized these people as destructive, dismissed them as marginal, or, at best, cast them as a harsh tonic for restoring vigor to decaying and soft agricultural societies from ancient Mesopotamia to Imperial Rome to Han China. In the 1950’s, a British archaeologist Mortimer Wheeler blamed the aggressive, chariot-driving Aryans who swept in from the steppes for the demise of the peaceful Indus River civilization after 1800 B.C., though later archaeologists dismissed that claim.
paragraphs.translationZh: （3）在过去的一个世纪里，学者们批评这些人具有破坏性，将他们视为边缘人，或者充其量将他们视为一种严厉的补品，可以为从古代美索不达米亚到罗马帝国再到汉朝的腐朽而软弱的农业社会恢复活力。 1950 年代，英国考古学家莫蒂默·惠勒 (Mortimer Wheeler) 将公元前 1800 年之后和平的印度河文明的灭亡归咎于从草原席卷而至、驾驶战车的雅利安人，但后来考古学家驳回了这一说法。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) But Michael Frachetti, a young archaeologist at Washington University in St.Louis, takes the radical view that Central Asians were early midwives in the birth of civilization rather than a destructive force. Frachetti argues that ancient pastoralists living in the third millennium B.C., at the time of the first great cities of Mesopotamia, Egypt, and the Indus, created a network stretching across thousands of miles that passed along goods, technologies, and ideas central to urban life. He believes they helped create civilization rather than hindering it.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 但圣路易斯华盛顿大学的年轻考古学家迈克尔·弗拉切蒂(Michael Frachetti)持激进观点，认为中亚人是文明诞生的早期助产士，而不是破坏性力量。弗拉切蒂认为，生活在公元前三千年的古代牧民，即美索不达米亚、埃及和印度河等第一座大城市的时代，创造了一个绵延数千英里的网络，传递城市生活的核心商品、技术和思想。他相信他们帮助创造了文明，而不是阻碍了它。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) Most archaeological work in Central Asia during the past century has focused on the open and rolling plains that stretch from the Black Sea to Manchuria. These steppes only came to life after 2000 B.C., when horse domestication and riding suddenly turned a forbidding landscape for pedestrians into a natural highway of grass.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 上个世纪中亚的大部分考古工作都集中在从黑海一直延伸到满洲的开阔而起伏的平原上。这些草原直到公元前 2000 年才开始生机勃勃，当时马匹的驯化和骑马突然将行人望而生畏的景观变成了天然的草地高速公路。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) By contrast, the areas to the south of the steppes have long been dismissed as backwaters of history. In the past, these southern mountains and deserts were considered too remote, rugged, and inhospitable to have played a role in early migrations or the emergence of urban life. The Karakum Desert, where it might rain once in a decade, covers nearly two-thirds of today’s Turkmenistan, while the perpetually snow-covered Tian Shan Mountains of western China and eastern Kyrgyzstan soar 24,000 feet into the thin air. It is there that Frachetti and a new generation of archaeologists from the United States and Central Asian nations are discovering evidence of a network of pastoralists who thrived centuries before hooves resounded on the steppes to the north. These forgotten peoples may have carried such markers of civilization as ceramics and grains across thousands of miles, two millennia before the Silk Road linked the Roman Empire with Han China. Frachetti argues that the new data emerging from the region force archaeologists to rethink their ideas about trade across Eurasia during the Bronze Age, when the first civilizations were taking form to the east, south, and west.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 相比之下，草原以南地区长期以来一直被视为历史的死水区。过去，这些南部山区和沙漠被认为过于偏远、崎岖和荒凉，在早期移民或城市生活的出现中没有发挥过作用。卡拉库姆沙漠十年一遇，覆盖了今天土库曼斯坦近三分之二的土地，而中国西部和吉尔吉斯斯坦东部常年冰雪覆盖的天山山脉高耸入云，高达 24,000 英尺。正是在那里，弗拉切蒂和来自美国和中亚国家的新一代考古学家正在发现证据，证明在马蹄声响彻北方大草原之前的几个世纪里，牧民网络就已经繁荣起来。这些被遗忘的民族可能已经带着陶瓷和谷物等文明标志跨越了数千英里，比丝绸之路将罗马帝国与汉族连接起来早了两千年。弗拉切蒂认为，该地区出现的新数据迫使考古学家重新思考他们对青铜时代欧亚大陆贸易的看法，当时第一个文明正在东部、南部和西部形成。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) Frachetti, who has studied modern-day pastoralists in such unforgiving landscapes as the Sahara and Scandinavia, was drawn to the southern region of Central Asia for its environmental diversity of desert, grassland, and meadows. Instead of a wasteland, he saw an ideal landscape for enterprising herders who wanted to pasture their animals in all seasons. Together with his colleagues, Frachetti began digging a decade ago in the Dzhungar Mountains of Kazakhstan. Covering nearly 500 square miles, this region lies between the Tian Shan and Altai mountain ranges, and boasts sharp peaks topping 12,000 feet, as well as harsh desert. At a site near a village called Begash, on a flat terrace enclosed by steep canyon walls alongside a small stream, the team uncovered the foundations of simple stone structures along with an array of potsherds (陶瓷碎片) and bronze and stone artifacts in stone-lined oval and rectangular tombs. The earliest layers at Begash date to at least as early as 2500 B.C., based on alpha magnetic spectrometry dating of organic remains, says Frachetti. One woman was laid to rest with a bell-shaped hooked bronze earring around 1700 B.C., according to electron spin resonance dating. Similar earrings are only found several centuries later some 600 miles to the north on the Siberian steppes, hinting at styles that moved north over time.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 弗拉切蒂研究了撒哈拉和斯堪的纳维亚半岛等恶劣地区的现代牧民，他被中亚南部地区沙漠、草原和草甸等环境多样性所吸引。他看到的不是一片荒地，而是一片适合有进取心的牧民四季放牧的理想景观。十年前，弗拉切蒂和他的同事开始在哈萨克斯坦的准噶尔山脉进行挖掘。该地区占地近 500 平方英里，位于天山山脉和阿尔泰山脉之间，拥有高达 12,000 英尺的尖峰和严酷的沙漠。在一个名为贝加什 (Begash) 的村庄附近的一处遗址上，在一条小溪旁被陡峭的峡谷壁包围的平坦露台上，研究小组在石砌的椭圆形和长方形坟墓中发现了简单石头结构的地基以及一系列陶片（陶瓷碎片）以及青铜和石制品。 Frachetti 表示，根据有机遗骸的 α 磁谱测定法测年，贝加什最早的地层至少可以追溯到公元前 2500 年。根据电子自旋共振年代测定，公元前 1700 年左右，一名妇女的墓中安葬着一枚钟形钩状青铜耳环。几个世纪后，在西伯利亚大草原以北约 600 英里处才发现了类似的耳环，这暗示着随着时间的推移，风格逐渐向北迁移。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) More surprisingly, the excavators found wheat, which was first domesticated in the Fertile Crescent of the Middle East, and broomcorn millet that was first widely grown in northern China. The grains were used ritually in a burial, and radiocarbon dating of the remains dates them to about 2200 B.C., making them the oldest known domesticated grains in Central Asia. The people of Begash may not have grown either grain — there are no grinding stones, a sign of grain preparation — but instead received it via trade networks stretching from the Near East to China.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 更令人惊讶的是，挖掘机发现了首先在中东新月沃地驯化的小麦和首先在中国北方广泛种植的黍。这些谷物在葬礼上被用于葬礼，根据遗骸的放射性碳测年，它们的年代可追溯到公元前 2200 年左右，这使它们成为中亚已知最古老的驯化谷物。贝加什人可能没有种植任何一种谷物——没有磨石，这是准备谷物的标志——而是通过从近东延伸到中国的贸易网络​​获得这些谷物。

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) Dorian Fuller, a leading expert in ancient grains based at University College London, calls the finds “important and well dated.” He adds that Chinese crops such as millet began to appear in southwest Asia around 1900
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 伦敦大学学院古代谷物领域的顶尖专家多里安·富勒 (Dorian Fuller) 称这些发现“重要且过时”。他补充说，1900年左右，小米等中国作物开始出现在西南亚

paragraphs.sourceText: B) C., a few centuries after they reached Begash, which could mean the passage through the mountain regions was a means of gradual transmission from east to west. Frachetti speculates that the grains may have been acquired from other tribes and used for ritual purposes, and then perhaps were passed on in turn to other pastoral peoples. (10) What makes the Begash discoveries so important is that previously this region was assumed to have been a land of scattered foragers (狩猎者) until steppe peoples trickled down into the area’s valleys and mountain ranges after 2000 B.C. But it is becoming evident that the people of Begash were not simple foragers, but sophisticated pastoralists who tended their flocks, much as people in the area still do today. The inhabitants did not begin to use horses until well into the second millennium B.C., and the varieties of sheep and goat found here today appear to be related to the varieties first domesticated thousands of years before in western Iran, near ancient Mesopotamia. This indicates that Begash was “at the crossroads of extremely wide networks among Eurasian communities by the third millennium B.C.,” asserts Frachetti. That doesn’t mean that traders traversed thousands of miles in this early period. Instead, the archaeologist envisions pastoralists taking their flocks to higher pastures in the summer, where they encountered neighbors from other valleys doing the same. Thus, ideas and technologies might have passed gradually through the mountain corridors of southern Central Asia. This corridor, Frachetti believes, may have been a key conduit for Bronze Age developments farther into East Asia and Mongolia.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) C.，在他们到达贝加什几个世纪后，这可能意味着穿过山区的通道是从东到西逐渐传播的一种方式。弗拉切蒂推测，这些谷物可能是从其他部落获得的，用于仪式目的，然后可能又被传给了其他游牧民族。 (10) 贝加什的发现之所以如此重要，是因为之前这个地区被认为是分散的狩猎者的土地，直到公元前 2000 年之后草原民族逐渐进入该地区的山谷和山脉。但越来越明显的是，贝加什人并不是简单的采集者，而是经验丰富的牧民，他们照料羊群，就像该地区的人们今天仍然在做的那样。直到公元前二千年，居民们才开始使用马，今天在这里发现的绵羊和山羊品种似乎与数千年前在伊朗西部靠近古代美索不达米亚的地区首次驯化的品种有关。弗拉切蒂断言，这表明“到公元前三千年，贝加什就处于欧亚社区极其广泛的网络的十字路口”。这并不意味着交易者在早期就已经走过了数千英里。相反，考古学家设想牧民在夏天将羊群带到更高的牧场，在那里他们遇到来自其他山谷的邻居也在做同样的事情。因此，思想和技术可能逐渐穿过中亚南部的山区走廊。弗拉切蒂认为，这条走廊可能是青铜时代发展深入东亚和蒙古的关键通道。

paragraphs.sourceText: What have the Romans ever done for us? Obviously the roads — the roads go without saying. Then, how about guidance for how to live in the 21st century? That seems less likely, but in fact the last few years have seen growing interest in the work of Roman Stoic philosophers who offered just that. One of them was Epictetus.
paragraphs.translationZh: 罗马人为我们做过什么？显然是道路——道路不言而喻。那么，如何指导21世纪的生活呢？这似乎不太可能，但事实上，在过去的几年里，人们对罗马斯多葛派哲学家的著作越来越感兴趣，他们提出了这一点。其中之一是爱比克泰德。

paragraphs.sourceText: Stoicism holds that the key to a good, happy life is the cultivation of an excellent mental state, which the Stoics identified with virtue and being rational. Two fundamental principles can both be found in the Handbook, a short work summarizing the ideas of Epictetus. The first is that some things are within our control and some are not, and that much of our unhappiness is caused by thinking that we can control things that, in fact, we can’t.
paragraphs.translationZh: 斯多葛派认为，美好、幸福生活的关键是培养良好的精神状态，斯多葛派将这种状态视为美德和理性。这本手册是一本总结爱比克泰德思想的简短著作，其中包含两个基本原则。首先，有些事情在我们的控制范围内，有些则不然，我们的不快乐很大程度上是因为我们认为我们可以控制事实上我们不能控制的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: What can we control? Epictetus argues that we actually control very little. We don’t control what happens to us, we can’t control what the people around us say or do, and we can’t even fully control our own bodies, which get damaged and sick and ultimately die without regard for our preferences. The only thing that we really control is how we think about things, the judgments we make about things.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们能控制什么？爱比克泰德认为，我们实际上控制的很少。我们无法控制发生在我们身上的事情，我们无法控制周围的人所说或所做的事情，我们甚至无法完全控制自己的身体，无论我们的喜好如何，它都会受损、生病并最终死亡。我们真正控制的唯一事情是我们如何思考事物，我们对事物做出的判断。

paragraphs.sourceText: This leads us to the second fundamental principle: it’s not things that upset us, but how we think about things. Things happen. We then make judgments about what happens. If we judge that something really bad has happened, then we might get upset, sad, or angry, depending on what it is. If we judge that something bad is likely to happen then we might get scared or fearful. All these emotions are the product of the judgments we make. Things in themselves are value neutral, for what might seem terrible to us might be a matter of indifference to someone else, or even welcomed by others. It’s the judgments we make that introduce value into the picture, and it’s those value judgments that generate our emotional responses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这引出了第二个基本原则：让我们心烦意乱的不是事情，而是我们看待事情的方式。事情发生了。然后我们对发生的事情做出判断。如果我们判断发生了非常糟糕的事情，那么我们可能会感到不安、悲伤或愤怒，具体取决于事情是什么。如果我们判断可能会发生不好的事情，那么我们可能会感到害怕或恐惧。所有这些情绪都是我们做出判断的产物。事物本身是价值中立的，因为对我们来说看似可怕的事情可能对其他人来说是冷漠的，甚至是受到他人欢迎的。正是我们做出的判断将价值引入了画面，而正是这些价值判断产生了我们的情绪反应。

paragraphs.sourceText: Happiness comes from correctly managing the world around you. There are many different philosophies you can subscribe to, and the one below is just another one.
paragraphs.translationZh: 幸福来自正确管理周围的世界。您可以认同许多不同的哲学，下面的只是另一种。

paragraphs.sourceText: CONQUER YOUR MIND
paragraphs.translationZh: 征服你的思想

paragraphs.sourceText: There are not many things we have complete control over in this world. However, our mind is potentially one of them. Barring your thoughts, emotions, process, and resulting actions are completely under your control.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这个世界上我们能完全掌控的事情并不多。然而，我们的思想可能是其中之一。除非你的想法、情绪、过程以及由此产生的行动完全在你的控制之下。

paragraphs.sourceText: Training your mind is an essential skill, like learning to walk. However, not many people are showing us how.
paragraphs.translationZh: 训练你的思维是一项基本技能，就像学习走路一样。然而，没有多少人向我们展示如何做到这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: You need to become a master of your own mind. Master musicians and race car drivers have spent thousands of hours learning how to operate a machine exactly how they wish. There are real physical limitations to those machines, but within those boundaries you can create incredible feats. And in your mind, you can change how you think. You can eliminate negativity, see solutions over problems, and connect with people. It takes work, failure, and repeated conditioning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你需要成为自己思想的主人。音乐大师和赛车手花费了数千个小时学习如何按照自己的意愿操作机器。这些机器确实存在物理限制，但在这些限制内，您可以创造令人难以置信的壮举。在你的脑海里，你可以改变你的想法。您可以消除消极情绪，找到问题的解决方案，并与人建立联系。这需要努力、失败和反复的调节。

paragraphs.sourceText: CONQUER YOUR BODY
paragraphs.translationZh: 征服你的身体

paragraphs.sourceText: Your body is simply an incredible tool to help you experience the world. It’s another machine in your life that you have to manage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您的身体只是一个令人难以置信的工具，可以帮助您体验世界。这是你生活中另一台需要你管理的机器。

paragraphs.sourceText: You don’t have to be a peak athlete or a fitness trainer. You do have to provide your body with quality food and exercise. It was originally so simple, because that is what we were made to do. You ate, you moved, and you were filled with unlimited energy. Unfortunately, our society has made it difficult. We’ve become addicted to short-term rewards and fast-food drugs that make daily healthy living uncomfortable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您不必是顶级运动员或健身教练。您确实必须为您的身体提供优质食物和锻炼。本来就是这么简单，因为那就是我们被造的目的。你吃，你动，你充满了无限的能量。不幸的是，我们的社会使它变得困难。我们已经沉迷于短期奖励和快餐药物，这让我们每天的健康生活变得不舒服。

paragraphs.sourceText: Break free from that, and be human again. Run, jump, fight, and eat real food. This also takes hard work. But remember, as you manage your mind, it will be much easier to manage your body.
paragraphs.translationZh: 摆脱它，重新成为人类。奔跑、跳跃、战斗，并吃真正的食物。这也需要艰苦的努力。但请记住，当你管理你的思想时，管理你的身体就会容易得多。
